audit.whatIsWrong: Every single row of the chart gave Graves the level, on both layers, with ratings of 2/10 and 3/10 — while diff already read FAV, the win rate is 55.99%, and all seven whys describe Mordekaiser winning (whys[3]: 'every extended melee fight is yours'; whys[4]: 'a near-guaranteed kill').
audit.why: The packet chart reads Skill / Mordekaiser x5 / Skill. The full layer was generated as if the lane were lost and nothing reconciled it against the content prose or the win rate, so a player opening this page was told the opposite of what the same page then explained.
audit.corrected: All seven rows set to the packet chart in both layers as one atomic group, with ratings inverted from the mirror's Graves-side 5,3,3,3,2,4,5 to 5,7,7,7,8,6,5.

audit.why: The spike set is right and unusually well chosen — it gives Graves his own entry at spikes[3] ('Lvl 6 (his)') rather than pretending he has none, which matches the mirror's read that his one fightable window is his first item on your R's cooldown.

audit.whatIsWrong: Quickdraw was given no cooldown and its cooldown-refund on basic attacks was never mentioned. Smoke Screen was called a 'blind' in whys[4] and spikes[1]. End of the Line's terrain behaviour was absent entirely.
audit.why: Quickdraw is 16/15/14/13/12 and Riot's text says hitting enemies with basic attacks lowers its cooldown and refreshes the resistance boost — so letting him free-hit the wave shortens the only window you have. Smoke Screen reduces sight range, it does not blind: your autos still land, you just cannot see him. End of the Line detonates on colliding with terrain, so standing near a wall makes his poke land a second early.
audit.corrected: Cooldown and the auto-refund written into dosFull[0].d and breakdown.cooldowns; the sight-range wording fixed in whys[4]; the terrain detonation into dontsFull[1].d.

audit.whatIsWrong: The missing-interactions file says Graves can cut your retreat with End of the Line because you have no dash. Riot's own Q text does not support that — the shell detonates after 1 second or on colliding with terrain; it does not create terrain.
audit.why: The kit file's derived 'terrain: creates terrain' flag misfires on this tooltip. The real, verifiable interaction is the opposite direction: walls make his shell go off sooner.
audit.corrected: Wrote the verifiable version (detonates early off walls) and did not write the wall-off-your-retreat claim anywhere.

edits.before: Realm of Death isolates him 1v1 with no Smoke Screen blind and no dash that helps — a near-guaranteed kill that flips any even lane.
edits.after: Realm of Death isolates him 1v1 where Smoke Screen has nothing to hide him from and Quickdraw has nowhere to go — the free kill.

edits.before: His dash + armor stacks. Engage when it's down. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: Quickdraw is 16s at rank 1, but his autos cut it — deny him free hits on the wave.

edits.after: - Quickdraw (E): 16s at rank 1, refreshed down by his autos — it stacks resists too, so trade after he spends it.

notes: All three flagged suspectNames are false positives — 'Hold Realm of Death', 'Use Realm of Death' and "Death's Grasp's" are the correct names with a verb or a possessive attached. The real defect was the full-layer chart, which gave Graves all seven rows at 2/10 on a 55.99% matchup already marked FAV. Only 33 games, so the win rate is thin, but the direction is not in doubt and the packet chart, the mirror and the page's own prose all agree. One thing left alone: spikes[1].text still says 'his Smoke Screen blind', which is the same sight-range-versus-blind error I fixed in whys[4] — it did not fit the length band without rewriting the whole sentence, and it is a wording error rather than a decision error. The Mordekaiser kit's 'grounding' flag on Q is unsupported by Riot's text, so I claimed nothing about Obliterate denying Quickdraw.
